subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Internal recruitment means filling a vacancy:
questions.explain: Internal recruitment promotes or transfers current staff; external recruitment hires from outside.

questions.q: Redundancy differs from dismissal because redundancy occurs when:
options: The job itself is no longer needed
questions.explain: Redundancy is losing a job because the role is no longer required, not due to employee fault.

questions.q: Induction training is provided:
options: To new employees when they start
questions.explain: Induction familiarises new staff with the organisation, role and procedures.

questions.q: Offshoring involves relocating a business process:
questions.explain: Offshoring moves activities abroad; outsourcing contracts them to a third party (which may be local).

questions.q: Span of control refers to the number of:
options: Subordinates directly reporting to a manager
questions.explain: Span of control is how many people report directly to one manager.

questions.q: Delayering means removing:
options: Layers of hierarchy, often middle management
questions.explain: Delayering flattens the structure by cutting hierarchical levels.

questions.q: A flat organisational structure typically has:
options: Few layers and wide spans of control
questions.explain: Flat structures have fewer levels and wider spans; tall structures have many levels and narrow spans.

questions.q: When branch managers are given authority to make their own decisions, the business is using:
questions.explain: Decentralisation passes decision-making down to lower levels or local units.

questions.q: An autocratic leader:
questions.explain: Autocratic leaders make decisions alone; democratic leaders consult; laissez-faire delegates freely.

questions.q: Laissez-faire leadership involves:
questions.explain: Laissez-faire leaders give staff autonomy with little direct supervision.

questions.q: Herzberg's two-factor theory distinguishes motivators from:
questions.explain: Motivators (e.g. achievement) drive satisfaction; hygiene factors (e.g. pay, conditions) prevent dissatisfaction.

questions.q: In Maslow's hierarchy of needs, esteem needs come:
questions.explain: Maslow's order: physiological, safety, social, esteem, self-actualisation.

questions.q: Taylor's scientific management assumed workers are motivated mainly by:
questions.explain: Taylor assumed economic motivation, using piece-rate pay and efficiency methods.

questions.q: Giving an employee more challenging and meaningful responsibilities is an example of:
questions.explain: Job enrichment adds depth and challenge to work, a non-financial motivator.

questions.q: Piece-rate pay links pay to:
questions.explain: Piece rate pays per unit of output, a financial motivator linked to productivity.

questions.q: Handy's cultural types include power, role, task and:
questions.explain: Charles Handy identified power, role, task and person cultures.

questions.q: A 'culture clash' is a particular risk during:
questions.explain: Combining firms with different corporate cultures can cause conflict (a culture clash).

questions.q: A barrier to effective communication could be:
questions.explain: Barriers include jargon, noise, language, and physical or hierarchical distance.

questions.q: Formal communication is communication that:
options: Follows official channels and the hierarchy
questions.explain: Formal communication uses recognised organisational channels; informal is the 'grapevine'.

questions.q: Collective bargaining is negotiation between:
options: Employers and trade unions representing employees
questions.explain: Collective bargaining negotiates pay and conditions between employers and employee representatives.

questions.q: Arbitration in an industrial dispute involves:
options: A neutral third party making a (often binding) decision
questions.explain: Arbitration uses an independent third party to resolve a dispute, unlike conciliation which only facilitates agreement.

specSource: IB Diploma Business Management guide (first assessment 2024); Unit 2 — Human resource management
